source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Non-parallel sides is the label that belongs on this item, so 'When does a trapezium have equal base angles?' is answered as non-parallel sides rather than isosceles trapezium.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Non-parallel sides is what produces isosceles trapezium, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about When does a trapezium have equal base angles?.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is isosceles trapezium because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'When does a trapezium have equal base angles?' as the operative test.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: isosceles trapezium is settled by running 'Which side lengths can be inferred in a parallelogram?': The opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal — on the item about When does a trapezium have equal base angles?.

intelligence.enrichment: When the non-parallel sides of a trapezium have equal lengths, it is an isosceles trapezium, and the angles opposite those equal sides are equal.
